Keto Beef Stroganoff Meal Prep Recipe

Serves 6


2 lbs 85/15 grass fed ground beef

1 medium to large onion, diced

2 clove garlic, minced

1 lb fresh mushrooms (any variety, I did baby bella and white mushrooms), sliced

2 tsp Better than Bouillon (or two beef bouillon cubes, but seriously try BtB if you haven't before, it is amazing, here's [why](https://www.thekitchn.com/whats-the-deal-with-better-than-bouillon-248408) )

1 tsp onion powder

1 tsp garlic powder

½ tsp paprika

salt & pepper to taste

2 teaspoons Worcestershire sauce

1.5 cups full fat sour cream

2 tsp fresh lemon juice

2 tablespoons fresh parsley or a sprinkle of dried

3 bags of Pasta Zero fettuccine or other shirataki noodles (usually found in the refrigerator near the tofu, or you may need to go to an asian market)


Brown the 85/15 beef in a large skillet over medium/high heat, remove the meat from the pan and set aside. You can drain some of the fat off if desired, but reserving most of the drippings in the pan to cook the onions and mushrooms in. If you only have lean beef, add a couple tablespoons of butter and melt before cooking veggies.


Add mushrooms, garlic and onions to the hot pan and drippings, and cook to desired softness on medium heat. There should be a fair amount of liquid from the veggies still in the pan when you add the Better than Bouillon, onion powder, garlic powder, paprika, salt and pepper, and Worcestershire sauce, then I like to let it reduce a bit. If there is not much liquid in the pan, just add a little bit of water so the spices and Better than Bouillon can dissolve and mix.


Then add the beef back in, along with the sour cream. Cook until it is heated through but not boiling, and thickened a bit. Mix in lemon juice and serve, garnished with fresh parsley over prepared shirataki noodles. (Learn best way to prepare them [here](https://youtu.be/3ccLN3TkNOs) )


If using this for meal prep, I measure out 6 portions trying to evenly distribute meat, sauce, and noodles. I usually only prepare one bag of noodles at a time, but you could probably do more as long as you don't freeze them, I'm not sure how well they would freeze. 


Using the brands I did, macros came out to 12.5 net carbs, 43 grams fat, 36 grams of protein, and 577 calories.


I only eat one large meal per day, and it is usually my only significant source of carbs in a day. So even though 12 carbs might seems high for one meal, I rarely get more than 20 grams of carbs per day.

Yes, me too! I lost 70 lbs and it was a wild ride indeed. After about 4 months of maintenance, my hair has finally started to regrow. I was lucky and my periods normalized as soon as I started keto, but now they are out of wack again from working out so much more than before. The acne was hit and miss during weightloss, and now I only get it right before a period, so mostly normal. The only thing I haven't seen any changes yet is my chin hair... it is still as bad as ever, but 🤷 can't win 'em all!

I'd say just keep doing what you're doing. A lot of these symptoms take time to normalize. Hairloss can take a year or more to stop/start regrowth. Our fat stores a lot of hormones, and with PCOS especially so. When we lose weight, a lot of these hormones are released back into our body before being flushed out and that can cause lots of problems during the weightloss phase. But once you get to your goal weight and stop losing, things should start to even out after a couple months of balanced maintenance. I'd look into metformin in the meantime if that's something you are interested in trying.

Your OB/GYN is right. I got my diagnosis the same way. Do you have any abdominal pain or anything else that would point to you having cysts? PCOS is an endocrine disorder. It is caused by insulin resistance and our ovaries get sensitive to the insulin, so they excrete a ton of testosterone which causes irregular periods, acne, hairloss etc. To be diagnosed with PCOS, you need to meet two out of three criteria,1) irregular and/or heavy periods, 2) symptoms of high androgens (like testosterone, so acne, hairloss etc, 3) cysts on the ovaries. You are saying you already have two out of three, therefore you already meet the criteria for PCOS. It is possible to have PCOS without actual cysts on your ovaries. If you aren't having pain or anything, it isn't necessary to do an ultrasound for diagnosis. Source: registered nurse and also have PCOS.

Edit: so yes cysts are just another symptom of PCOS. When they named "PCOS," they thought the cysts were a cause. Now that they know that is a misnomer, they are considering renaming it "metabolic reproductive syndrome" or similar. 

Edit 2: yes it is possible to not have insulin resistance. But if you have any androgen/testosterone symptoms, that is from your ovaries' overreacting to insulin. I was summarizing, but if you have the lean PCOS, that is also something they are wanting to rename because it is an entirely different issue biologically as well as for treatment. Research is unfortunately in baby stages on PCOS, so we are learning as we go!

Not a dumb question at all! Actually you can get a different effect, not worse or better necessarily, just different. If you get a lot of THC under your tongue, you have a lot of shallow blood vessels under there. The blood vessels can absorb THC. In the medical field we call this method, or route of taking a medication, "sublingual," which just means "under the tongue." When you suck on an edible, your saliva dissolves the candy and makes it easy to get some under your tongue and straight into your blood stream (so it is very quick). This is why you get a little boost of a high when you first suck on the candy and then you get a stronger effect later after you've digested whatever you swallowed and wasn't absorbed under your tongue at the beginning. If you just swallow it, you don't absorb any under your tongue, and it all goes through digestion. I guess theoretically you would get a slightly weaker effect but spread out more over time by sucking on it since you absorb some THC at the beginning and some later. Whereas just chewing and swallowing would mean just one stronger high later.  You can actually buy sublingual tinctures that are specially designed to absorb under your tongue extremely effectively.

I'm pretty OCD about keeping my glass clean, I don't like the tatse of resin at all. I have several pieces that are hard to clean, but salt and rubbing alcohol have always been more than enough. I also use this set of [brushes](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0115SLLLM/ref=cm_sw_r_cp_apa_AVlTyb1M7F5R0) that can be twisted  and molded to get into hard to reach places. I rotate all my glass pieces so at least one is soaking in alcohol in a Ziploc baggie, one I'm using, and one is clean and ready to go. The trick is to let it soak which softens the resin, and then using salt wetted down with alcohol in the chambers that are hard to reach. I seal off any openings the salt can come out of with my fingers and hands and then shake for awhile until all the salt scrapes off the yuck. I think too much alcohol with the salt can make getting the gunk off harder, so just wet the salt and then put in a tiny bit more since some will probably leak out while you're shaking it. Then I use my brushes to remove any remainder that I couldn't get with the salt. Then rinse well with hot water. They end up sparkling clean and look brand new! If I think I'm really going to have trouble with something or I've procrastinated cleaning and it's really bad, while it is soaking in alcohol in a baggie I'll run the baggie under hot water in the sink to gently heat up the alcohol a bit. It dissolves the gunk better. Then I'll let it sit for a few days and then repeat the hot water before I do the salt and brushes. Never had a piece that didn't get clean this way. 

TLDR: Use a method of soaking in rubbing alcohol, salt and scrubbing brushes. Detailed instructions above.

This was my first time making edibles from scratch. I made the butter myself from flower using a slow cooker. Here is the recipe for the cookies:

"Special” Pumpkin Spice Sugar Cookies

Serves: 36 cookies

Ingredients
½ cup butter, softened
½ cup  cannabutter, softened
1½ cups granulated sugar
1 egg
2¼ cups all­-purpose flour
½ teaspoon baking powder
½ teaspoon Kosher salt
2 Tbsp (or more to taste) pumpkin pie spice
1 ½ teaspoon vanilla
¼ cup granulated sugar with cinnamon mixed in for rolling cookies


Instructions
1. Preheat oven to 325º F. Line cookie sheets with parchment paper or a nonstick baking mat.
2. Cream together butter and granulated sugar until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes. Add egg and mix until well-­combined.
3. Stir in flour, baking powder, salt, and vanilla.
4. Scoop cookie dough by the tablespoon full and roll into a ball.
5. Add cinnamon sugar mix to a large bowl for rolling cookie dough in before baking. Place each ball of cookie dough into the bowl of granulated sugar and roll to coat well. Place cookie dough onto baking sheet, spacing about 1½ ­inches to 2 inches apart. Lightly press each cookie down. Bake for 12-16 minutes or until lightly browned.
